---
title: "Semantics registry"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

The registry lists SAS behaviours that commonly differ from base R defaults
and records whether sasonr reproduces them. The status comes from the
offline conformance cases (gold standard: SAS 9.4).

* **verified**: all linked cases match SAS.
* **partial**: some cases match; the unverified situations stop with
  `sasonr_unsupported`.
* **unsupported**: not implemented yet; using it stops the program.

```{r}
reg <- utils::read.csv(system.file("registry", "semantics.csv", package = "sasonr"),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("Entries: %d (verified %d, partial %d, unsupported %d, not applicable %d)",
            nrow(reg), sum(reg$sasonr_status == "verified"),
            sum(reg$sasonr_status == "partial"),
            sum(reg$sasonr_status == "unsupported"),
            sum(reg$sasonr_status %in% c("n/a", "not_applicable", "na"))))
```

```{r}
knitr::kable(reg[, c("entry", "kind", "sas_behaviour", "r_default", "sasonr_status", "cases", "cases_pass")],
             col.names = c("Entry", "Kind", "SAS behaviour", "R default", "sasonr", "Cases", "Pass"))
```

The list of entries was collected from published SAS 9.4 documentation and R
documentation; the descriptions, the statuses and the cases behind them are
sasonr's own.

## Ordering of missing values

The most common silent difference between SAS and R is sort order. SAS sorts
numeric missing values in a fixed hierarchy that runs *before* every non-missing
number, and reverses it under `DESCENDING`:

| | ascending | descending |
|---|---|---|
| numeric | `._` < `.` < `.A` < … < `.Z` < any number (including `-1e300`) | the exact reverse |
| character | blank < non-blank, compared byte by byte | the exact reverse |

The character rule is byte collation, not the locale collation that
`order()`/`sort()` use in R, so a translated sort cannot simply call
`arrange()`. `PROC SORT`, the `BY` statement and the merge machinery all use
this order; `tests/testthat/test-proc.R` pins it down.
